# TEKEVER provenance evidence — SRC-0335

Buyer-supplied box-label photograph visibly shows service tag `G21FTJ4`, `QTY 20`, `To # 001`, Dell order `1033632603`, customer-PO data and a May-coded label. The underside photograph shows a `TEKEVER` asset sticker on the same described device. These materially corroborate corporate-batch origin but do not prove lawful disposal or the reseller's title.

TEKEVER's official company site identifies it as a Portuguese Defence and Security company building AI-driven autonomous and dual-use systems, not merely a generic security-services firm:

- https://www.tekever.com/about/

Because the device visibly belonged to a corporate fleet, Windows Autopilot/Intune/Entra deregistration is a purchase gate. Microsoft states that a device permanently leaving an organization should be removed from Intune and deregistered from Autopilot; Dell likewise states that deregistration must cover Autopilot, Intune and Entra rather than only one layer:

- https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/autopilot/registration-overview
- https://www.dell.com/support/kbdoc/en-us/000132036/replacement-hardware-bound-to-windows-autopilot

The combination of an apparently recent batch, asset sticker and private resale is compatible with legitimate surplus, auction, liquidation, logistics or insurance channels, but also with unauthorized diversion. No conclusion is possible without an original invoice or auction/liquidation receipt linking TEKEVER/the authorized disposer to the current seller, explicit organizational deregistration and accepted Dell ownership transfer.
